- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.33), model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–2% to avoid missing downside risk.
- Model consistently overreacts to recent spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days) — cap forecast peak at 2–3% above prior high.
- After a sharp price drop, model often fails to recognize mean reversion; add 0.5–1.5% upward bias in next 3–5 days if sentiment is neutral or mildly positive.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles (e.g., +0.33, -0.33, +0.67), model tends to lag; shift forecast 1–2 days ahead with slight downward bias.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates early in the period; apply 1–2% downward correction for first 7–10 days if sentiment is mixed or negative.
- If sentiment is consistently low (≤ 0.33) over 3+ days, model underestimates; add 0.5–1.5% upward bias to avoid missing support levels.
